exposure: Emergency cesarean section for fetal distress
outcome: Neonatal morbidity (defined as a 5-minute Apgar score <7, need for mechanical ventilation, admittance to a neonatal intensive care unit, or respiratory insufficiency symptoms)
cohort: 61 parturients undergoing emergency cesarean section for fetal distress
finding: While regional anesthesia was associated with some improved outcomes (shorter hospitalization, higher umbilical cord blood pH), the study found no statistically significant difference between regional and general anesthesia in terms of neonatal morbidity for emergency cesarean sections due to fetal distress.
